key_insight: TrajectoryFlowNet learns both how particles move and how fluid flows from very limited trajectory measurements. It connects particle-level motion with a flow-field view to predict long-range paths.
problem_solved: Reconstructing flow fields and predicting long-range particle trajectories when only sparse measurements of particle motion are available.
method: Uses a physics-informed learning model to infer particle trajectories and flow fields together.
Connects the Lagrangian view of moving particles with the Eulerian view of fluid motion across space.
Validates the approach in simulations and blood-flow experiments.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work illustrates how physical knowledge can support learning from scarce measurements. Joint trajectory and flow prediction could help analyze fluid systems where dense measurements are difficult to obtain.
visual_elements: Sparse measured particle positions expanding into predicted long-range trajectories.
Side-by-side views of particle paths and a flow-field map, labeled Lagrangian and Eulerian.
A pipeline diagram: limited trajectory measurements → physics-informed TrajectoryFlowNet → trajectories and flow fields.
Paired illustrations of simulation and blood-flow experimental validation.
paper_title: Lagrangian–Eulerian learning of flow field and trajectories with TrajectoryFlowNet
paper_authors: Jingdi Wan, Hongping Wang, Bo Liu, Xiaolei Yang, Xiaodong Hu
